en: We pay homage to the Sage Vairocana, who is white in luster, born from the syllable Oṃ, seated upon a central lion-throne, and endowed with the three mudrās of awakening. (1)
We pay homage to the glorious Akṣobhya, who has the luster of blue arising from the syllable *hūṃ*, who is seated upon an elephant in the east, and who is endowed with the earth-touching mudrā. (2)
I bow to Ratnasaṃbhava, who is born from the syllable TRĀṂ, who has the luster of gold, who is mounted upon a horse to his right, and who is endowed with the boon-granting mudrā.
We praise the Lord Amitābha-muni, who has arisen from the syllable *jhiṃ*, possesses a reddish luster, sits upon a peacock-throne in the west, and bears the form of meditative absorption. (4)
I bow to Amoghasiddhi, who has the dark-blue luster produced from the sound "khaṅ," who is seated upon Garuḍa in the north, and who is joined with the gesture of granting fearlessness. || 5 ||
Homage, homage to the four goddesses—Rocanā, Māmakī, Pāṇḍarā, and Tāraṇī—who are situated in the corners beginning with Brahmā. || 6 ||
We pay homage to Vajrasattva, the deity who is stainless, formless, whose nature is the light of individual self-awareness, and who resides within the heart-center (caitya). || 7 ||
The hymn of the syllables of the mantra of the venerable Lord Buddha is completed.
